summary: C-SCOPE accurately distinguishes the separate local and fresh CI runs, matches the frozen runner and finite serialized Chromium guarantees, and avoids fourth-renderer, generic-compiler, production-service, and concurrency claims. The future-renderer contract matches the Go-generated v1 profile and requires renderer conformance plus composition replay. Fresh report/log/archive hashes and all ten PR workflow outcomes are supported; published head binding relies on captured CI metadata because its object is absent locally.
limits: The evidence covers the recorded Linux CI toolchain and serialized Chromium profile only.
Published PR head/tree provenance relies on captured CI/publication metadata; the head Git object is unavailable locally.
No new application/session factory, independent oracle, generic compiler, fourth renderer, production service, or concurrency guarantee is established.
